resources.title: Binary search: visual notes
resources.summary: A step-by-step guide to sorted arrays, midpoint selection, boundary updates, and common off-by-one errors.
resources.body: Start with low = 0 and high = n − 1. Pick a midpoint. If the target is smaller, set high = mid − 1. If it is larger, set low = mid + 1. Stop when low > high. The loop is O(log n) because each step halves the remaining range.

resources.title: When sorted data helps
resources.summary: See how ordering turns a linear scan into repeated half-range decisions.
resources.body: A sorted list carries information about every value around the midpoint. This walkthrough compares linear scan and binary search on the same list and explains the prerequisite: the data must be sorted.

resources.title: Boundary conditions cheatsheet
resources.summary: Keep inclusive bounds consistent and avoid repeated midpoints.
resources.body: For inclusive bounds use low = 0, high = n − 1. Continue while low <= high. When target > array[mid], low = mid + 1. When target < array[mid], high = mid − 1.

resources.title: Binary search practice set
resources.summary: Try target present, absent, and edge-value cases with instant feedback.
resources.body: Practice three arrays: target at the first value, target at the final value, and target absent. Explain why each boundary update keeps all possible answers in the search range.
